To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the public needs to be educated to understand genomic information, (2) genomic information may improve risk communication and health behaviors, and (3) genomic information may provide new intervention targets.

the public health research community needs to: (1.) anticipate directions of genomic discoveries and take an agnostic perspective to frame research questions; (2.) focus on the three major risk factors that contribute to the top four diseases; and (3.) consider multiple levels of influences on these risk behaviors and systems that contribute.

(1) genomic discovery has the potential to improve public health; (2) communication, behavioral, social sciences research is needed to realize this potential; (3) research should address the three risk factors that contribute to the major chronic diseases that cause most deaths in the world; (4) the research should focus on the three areas identified in this article; and (5) research in these three areas should be informed by the crosscutting themes we identified.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how people understand, use and are affected by genomic information.

the social and behavioral aspects of genomic science and its application in the health care system, and we seek to understand how the public and health care professionals respond to the information and technology that are being developed.
how the social, economic, and political context of the health care system influences the health care system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
genomic information has the potential to be a valuable public health resource, but the research agenda for translating that promise into practice is only beginning to be defined.

genomic discovery has great promise for improving public health, and that the research agenda proposed here will help to realize this promise by providing evidence on the most efficient, effective, and acceptable ways to translate genomic discoveries into public health interventions.

the communication, behavioral and social sciences have a vital role in helping to translate the discoveries and products of the Human Genome Project and related research into public health applications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
genomic information has the potential to improve health and reduce health care costs, but only if it is effectively communicated and translated into action.

the research agenda should focus on how to best translate the genomic revolution into public health applications, and that this research should be conducted in a way that is responsive to the public's needs, concerns, and values.
the communication, behavioral and social sciences have much to offer in translating the promise of genomic discovery into improved health.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the communication, behavioral and social sciences can and should be an integral component of genomic research.
the communication, behavioral and social sciences research community is well positioned to play a key role in helping to realize the promise of the genomic revolution for public health.
the public health community needs to be proactive and anticipate how genomics research may be used to address public health problems.
